title: Addition & Subtraction
description: Class 3 IMO — Addition and subtraction of 3- and 4-digit numbers with and without regrouping, checking subtraction by addition, estimation and word problems.

topics.title: Addition With and Without Regrouping
topics.concept:
To add large numbers, line up the Ones, Tens, Hundreds and Thousands and add each column from the right. When a column adds up to 10 or more, we regroup (carry) 1 to the next column.

For 2,567 + 1,848: ones 7 + 8 = 15 (write 5, carry 1), tens 6 + 4 + 1 = 11 (write 1, carry 1), hundreds 5 + 8 + 1 = 14 (write 4, carry 1), thousands 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. The sum is 4,415.

examples.solution: No carrying: ones 7, tens 7, hundreds 8, thousands 4 → 4,877.
With carrying at each step the sum is 4,415.

recap: Add column by column from the Ones place.
If a column makes 10 or more, carry 1 to the next column.

topics.title: Subtraction With Borrowing & Checking
topics.concept:
To subtract, line up the places and subtract each column from the right. When the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next column.

We can check a subtraction by adding the answer to the number we subtracted — it should give back the first number. For 645 − 278 = 367, check: 367 + 278 = 645.
recap: Borrow 1 from the next column when the top digit is too small.
Check subtraction: answer + number subtracted = first number.

quiz.explanation: Check: 454 + 458 = 912, so the answer is correct.

topics.title: Estimation & Word Problems
topics.concept:
Estimation gives a quick, close answer. To estimate a sum or difference, first round each number to the nearest ten or hundred, then add or subtract. For example, 312 + 489 is about 300 + 500 = 800.

In word problems, words like in all and altogether mean add, while left, remaining and how many more mean subtract.

examples.solution: 467 is closer to 500 than to 400, so it rounds to 500.

examples.problem: A shop sold 1,245 items in the morning and 2,180 in the evening. How many in all?

recap: Round to the nearest ten/hundred, then estimate.
'In all' means add; 'left / how many more' means subtract.

quiz.explanation: The ones digit 8 is 5 or more, so 738 rounds up to 740.

quiz.q: A box has 156 red and 248 blue beads. How many beads in all?

questions.explanation: The same digits with one extra zero give 400.

questions.q: Which sum is NOT equal to 600?

questions.explanation: With carrying at each column, the sum is 6,023.
The tens digit 6 is 5 or more, so it rounds up to 1,300.

questions.q: A library had 3,450 books and bought 1,275 more. How many books now?
Amit had ₹5,000 and spent ₹3,650. How much is left?
Two villages have 2,345 and 1,890 people. What is the total population?
A number added to 1,250 gives 4,000. What is the number?
A shopkeeper had ₹5,000. He spent ₹1,250 on rice and ₹1,800 on oil. How much is left?
